references.text: Moses proclaimed that the Lord would raise up a prophet whom the people should listen to. Abraham points out that they have 'Moses and the prophets' – that is, the Torah and the writings of the prophets – as guidance, just as Moses himself delivered God's word to the people ([ref:5 Mos 18:15-19|Deuteronomy 18:15-19]).

Moses wrote down the words of the law in a book and gave it to the Levites as a testimony. This emphasizes that 'Moses' in Luke 16:29 refers to the writings Moses left behind ([ref:5 Mos 31:24-26|Deuteronomy 31:24-26]).

Isaiah urges the people to hold fast to 'the law and the testimony' – that is, Moses and the prophets – as a standard. This aligns with Abraham's statement that they have Moses and the prophets to listen to ([ref:Jes 8:20|Isaiah 8:20]).

The prophet Isaiah encourages seeking in the Lord's book and reading, for none of His words shall be lacking. This supports the idea that Scripture's testimony is sufficient ([ref:Jes 34:16|Isaiah 34:16]).

Jesus says that people examine the Scriptures because they believe they have eternal life in them, and it is these very writings that testify about Him. This confirms that Moses and the prophets, which Abraham refers to, point forward to Christ ([ref:Joh 5:39|John 5:39]).

Jesus says that Moses himself wrote about Him, and whoever does not believe Moses' writings will not believe Jesus' words either. This is closely connected with Abraham's point: they have Moses and the prophets – that should be enough ([ref:Joh 5:45-47|John 5:45-47]).

James in Acts mentions that from ancient times, Moses has had those who proclaim him in the cities, as he is read aloud in the synagogues every Sabbath. This shows the continuous access the people had to Moses' writings ([ref:Apg 15:21|Acts 15:21]).
The Jews in Berea examined the Scriptures daily to see if what Paul proclaimed was true. They used exactly Moses and the prophets as a test, just as Abraham recommends ([ref:Apg 17:11|Acts 17:11]).

Paul testifies that he says nothing other than what Moses and the prophets have said should happen. This confirms that Moses and the prophets contain the necessary message of salvation ([ref:Apg 26:22|Acts 26:22]).

The risen Jesus began with Moses and all the prophets and explained to the disciples what was written about Him in all the Scriptures. This shows that 'Moses and the prophets' testify about Christ and provide sufficient guidance, as Abraham claims ([ref:Luk 24:27|Luke 24:27]).

Paul writes to Timothy that the holy Scriptures are able to make one wise for salvation, and that all Scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching. This supports Abraham's point that Scripture (Moses and the prophets) is sufficient ([ref:2 Tim 3:15-17|2 Timothy 3:15-17]).
